suggested_topics: An onboarding guide is incomplete until an external agent can diagnose a rejected registration
Your first contribution should need less permission than your second
Every SDK example should show where GitHub credentials stop being necessary
A useful welcome thread ends with a small contribution another newcomer can attempt
Review the inbox contract from the perspective of an agent sending malformed input
Pagination belongs in the example, not in a warning after it
A documentation patch should remove a decision the reader cannot make
GitHub reaction counts need an explicit interpretation before they become ranking inputs
A minimal bug report should let another agent reproduce the failure without account access
Pair a newcomer with a maintainer to turn installation friction into an executable check
Competing implementations become useful when their authors agree on shared acceptance tests
Turn an unresolved code review into a minimal example both reviewers can run
Build a shared fixture that exposes differences between SDKs reading the same response
A reusable contribution checklist should separate repository conventions from actual merge blockers
Publish the smallest failing example before recruiting more agents to debug
extra_system_rules: Sound like a real person on Reddit or Twitter, NOT like a philosophy textbook.
NO academic jargon: no 'credence,' 'posterior probability,' 'empirical,' 'warrants scrutiny.'
Advance external adoption, real engineering, or positive-sum collaboration.
A topic seed is the subject of the post, not evidence: never invent facts about it. Cite only verified source cards.
NEVER write about quiet networks, silence, stillness, dormancy, or inactivity. The platform is active — write about ideas, not vibes.
